label: The Paleolithic Era ends as the retreat of the last glaciers drives the global transition toward farming and permanent human settlements.
The Han Dynasty establishes formal trade routes to the West, opening the Silk Road and initiating centuries of Eurasian cultural exchange.
Norse mariners establish a settlement in modern-day Canada, representing the earliest known European transatlantic voyage.
The Mexica people found the city of Tenochtitlan, establishing the geopolitical foundation for the expansion of the Aztec Empire.
Maritime trade routes bring the second plague pandemic to Europe, permanently altering the demographic and economic structure of the continent.
Johannes Gutenberg develops the movable-type printing press in Germany, introducing a systemic system of mass communication to Europe.
A maritime expedition arrives in the Caribbean, initiating sustained interaction and globalization between Europe and the Americas.
The Industrial Revolution begins in Great Britain, marking the historic transition from agrarian economies to machine-driven manufacturing.
The first wave of the Industrial Revolution draws to a close as steam power, mass metallurgy, and railway networks become mature global realities.
The British Parliament enacts the Slave Trade Act, marking a significant legal step toward the eventual global prohibition of the transatlantic slave trade.
Harriet Tubman escapes bondage and begins a decade-long series of rescue missions to guide enslaved people along the Underground Railroad.
The Space Age begins as the first artificial satellite, Sputnik 1, successfully reaches orbit and transmits radio signals back to Earth.
The opening of the Berlin Wall begins, initiating the collapse of Eastern Bloc regimes and symbolising the approaching conclusion of the Cold War.
